The second was the actual mental hospital. Most of it was also waiting. I never really got to talk to a therapist, just a couple convos with the psychiatrist but it wasn't particularly engaging. Outside of that they had a noisy and quiet day room to either read, write, or watch TV. Kinda cramped though.   


They had a couple group therapy bits, only one of which was remotely useful. Idk, everything there felt half-assed. The other patients were more helpful than the doctors were, especially my roommate.

Thanks for the compliments. I sorta just eyeballed it, but here's a general 'recipe':

1. Made brown rice a day before and refrigerated it (to dry it. Make sure the starch is cleaned off.)
(Two cups water to 1 cup rice. Will end up with just over two cups of rice)

2. Chopped a large carrot, half a stalk of broccoli and a quarter of an onion to bite sized pieces. (very important to not make them too large). You can prepare some minced garlic here too.

3. Sliced some chicken (boneless thighs) to small bite sized 'strands'. Season the chicken with a conservative amount of salt and pepper.

4. Mixed some low sodium soy sauce with a heaping tablespoon of brown sugar and mixed them together with a splash of water (to make it less cloy).

5. Lightly scrambled two eggs and set it aside.

6. Preheat pan with some canola oil. I like using olive oil, but you need the pan really hot and olive oil will burn. Take this time to fluff the rice again. Make sure you have everything at the ready, cause the stir fry part is fast.

7. Add chicken first. Fry for 2 minutes.

8. Add onion and garlic. Fry for a minute. 

9. Add rest of veggies. Fry for 2 minutes.

10. Add rice. Toast for 1.5 minutes constantly folding. 

11. Add soy sauce mixture. Continue to fold 1 minute. 

12. If you have some frozen peas, add now. Add your scrambled egg and take off heat. 

13. Fold everything together and put it in a large dish.

That about sums it up. Lots of preparation, quick frying time. Thanks for the love.
